name: Schema-Dependent Encoding Pathways
higher_order_principle: Prior knowledge (schemas) fundamentally alter the encoding pathway. Schema-congruent information is rapidly integrated via vmPFC-mediated neocortical pathway with reduced hippocampal involvement. Schema-incongruent information triggers strong hippocampal encoding via PE. Schema-irrelevant information is poorly encoded by both pathways. This three-way split means that the same instructional method has different effects depending on what the learner already knows.
transferable_to: expert vs novice instruction (experts need different methods)
organizational change management (framing change within existing schemas)

causal_links.key_evidence: van Kesteren et al., 2012; Tse et al., 2007; Tse et al., 2011

parameters.vmPFC_role: detects match between new input and existing neocortical schema
parameters.congruent: vmPFC facilitates rapid neocortical integration (bypasses hippocampus)
parameters.incongruent: vmPFC detects mismatch → signals hippocampus for strong PE-driven encoding
parameters.irrelevant: no schema activated → neither pathway strongly engaged

parameters.speed: fast — can integrate within a single exposure
parameters.memory_quality: gist-like, semantic (knows the fact but may not remember the learning episode)
parameters.instructional_implication: lecture and direct instruction CAN work for schema-congruent material because the existing schema does the organizational work

causal_links.key_evidence: van Kesteren et al., 2012; Greve et al., 2017

parameters.PE_strength: HIGH — violation of existing schema produces large PE
parameters.memory_quality: detailed, episodic (remembers the surprising information AND the context of learning it)
parameters.instructional_implication: MUST first activate the incorrect schema, THEN present the correcting information. Conceptual change pedagogy: 'predict → test → confront → resolve.' Prediction errors at the schema level are the most powerful encoding events.

MUST provide scaffolding — an organizational framework, advance organizer (Ausubel), or analogy — BEFORE presenting details. Create the schema first, then new information becomes schema-congruent or schema-incongruent (both encode better than irrelevant).

scope_conditions: Schemas are individual — each learner has different prior knowledge, so the same information is congruent for one learner and incongruent for another
Schema strength modulates: strong schemas produce stronger congruence/incongruence effects; weak schemas are more like schema-irrelevant
vmPFC is the SAME node identified as the architectural neuroscience bottleneck — further evidence for vmPFC as a domain-general regulatory hub
moderators: vmPFC_integrity (aging or damage impairs schema use)

interactions.description: E4 (vmPFC) acts as a switch that determines whether E1 (hippocampus) is strongly engaged (for incongruent) or bypassed (for congruent).
T1 is sensory PE; E4 involves conceptual/semantic PE. The computational principle is identical, operating at different levels of the hierarchy.

key_references: van Kesteren, M. T. R., et al. (2012). How schema and novelty augment memory formation. Trends in Neurosciences
Tse, D., et al. (2007). Schemas and memory consolidation. Science
Tse, D., et al. (2011). Schema-dependent gene activation and memory encoding in neocortex. Science
Greve, A., et al. (2017). Schema-based facilitation of memory consolidation. Nature Communications
